---
title: "Downloads & Replication"
---

Everything published here is the CONDLA team's own work: the coded dataset and its indices, the codebook, and the script that computes them. We do not publish the primary sources (legislation, operational manuals, press clippings) used to code each program.

## Files

- [**Dataset for exploring (CSV, 336×49)**](data/condla_indices.csv) — `condla_indices.csv`: the 36 coded variables plus the 4 severity indices and 5 vagueness indices, documented in [Codebook & Methodology](codebook.qmd). Same content as the replication dataset below, just under a shorter filename (it's the one used by [Explore the Data](explorar.qmd)).
- [**Dataset for replication (CSV)**](<descargas/Base%20de%20datos%20con%20variables%20orig%20e%20indices%20cond%20y%20vague%20%2849%20variables%29%202026.csv>) — same content, under the original filename expected by the replication script below.
- [**Full codebook (PDF)**](descargas/CONDLA_indices_codebook_v1.pdf) — `CONDLA_indices_codebook_v1.pdf`: the definition of every one of the 49 columns and the mathematical derivation of the indices.
- [**Replication script (Quarto/R)**](descargas/Script_publicable_CONDLA_v1.qmd) — `Script_publicable_CONDLA_v1.qmd`: rebuilds the 9 index columns from the 36 coded variables.

## How to replicate the index calculation

1. Install [R](https://cran.r-project.org/) and the `tidyverse` package (`install.packages("tidyverse")`). Optionally, [RStudio](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/) or [Positron](https://positron.posit.co/) to open the `.qmd` with an interface.
2. Download the **script** and the **replication dataset** (the two links marked above) into the same folder, without renaming them.
3. Open `Script_publicable_CONDLA_v1.qmd` and render it (the *Render* button in RStudio/Positron, or `quarto render Script_publicable_CONDLA_v1.qmd` from the terminal).
4. The script recomputes the 9 index columns (`cond_edu`, `cond_health`, ..., `conditionality`, `av_vagueness`) from scratch and writes them back to the same CSV — the result should be identical to what is published here.

Questions, or requests for the underlying database (before it was reduced to the analytical sample): please contact the researchers, see [Team](equipo.qmd).
